official.status_note: The official programme page still publishes the 2025 call, which closed on 30 April 2025; no newer call was published on campusfrance.org at verification time.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Holders in public institutions under the Ministry of Higher Education are exempted from administrative registration fees for a national degree; the programme states course fees are not covered, and CROUS residence rent remains the holder's responsibility.
benefits: Payment of a half-yearly allowance of EUR 6,850, transferred semi-annually to a bank account opened in France (RIB to be sent to Campus France)
Payment of an installation allowance of EUR 1,700, available in cash at a Western Union counter upon arrival in France
Exemption from administrative registration fees for a national degree in universities and public institutions under the supervision of the Ministry of Higher Education
Priority assistance in finding accommodation in CROUS university residences, with rent paid by the scholarship holder

Enrolment in an insurance plan for the first three months of the stay (pending enrolment in the French social security system) for holders without a European Health Insurance Card, plus enrolment in supplemental health insurance
Exemption from the CVEC (Contribution de Vie Etudiante et de Campus) and special discounts on cultural activities organised by Campus France
eligibility: National of one of the 26 eligible EU member states: Germany, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Croatia, Denmark, Spain, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Czech Republic, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Sweden
Students of French nationality, including bi-nationals, are not eligible
At least 18 years old when the mobility period in France begins; no upper age limit provided the applicant does not already possess a master's degree from any country
Admitted to a French higher education institution in Master 1 or Master 2 for the relevant academic year
Not the holder of a French higher education degree and not currently registered in France for a higher education degree
Not a recipient of an Erasmus+, AUF or other French ministry scholarship
requirements: The letter of admission must be sent as soon as it is received by the candidate

If no admission letter is held at application time, a sworn statement must be attached for each choice of course, naming the institution and the anticipated programme, together with a copy of the correspondence showing the admission application is being processed
Diplomas and transcripts must be translated into French or English
The application file must be sent electronically to the French Embassy in the country of nationality
documents: 'France Excellence Europa Scholarship' application form, duly completed and signed
CV and cover letter, in French or English
Copy of the most recent higher education diploma obtained, or of the secondary school diploma if the applicant is still in higher education (translated)
Copies of transcripts from the last two years of higher education (translated)
Copy of an identity document (passport or ID card)
Letter of admission to a Master 1 or Master 2 programme at a French institution, or a sworn statement plus correspondence per intended programme
selection_criteria: Awarded on the basis of academic excellence and in line with the strategic priorities of the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
Applications are pre-selected by the college relations teams at the French embassies
They are then evaluated within the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs by collaboration specialists from the eligible fields
coverage: Exemption from administrative registration fees for a national degree in public institutions; the programme explicitly does not cover course fees, nor international or national transportation
application_method: Candidates send their applications electronically to the French Embassy in their country of nationality, using the country-specific Campus France email address published on the programme page (fee.<country>@campusfrance.org)
2025 round reference timeline: embassy pre-selection 2-13 May 2025, selection committees 14-23 May 2025, notification of results from 26 May 2025, completion of the final list in July 2025
official.application_route: Email the complete application file to the French Embassy in your country of nationality by the published deadline; there is no separate online application portal.
official.citizenship_residency: National of one of the 26 listed EU member states; French nationals, including bi-nationals, are excluded.
official.international_eligibility: Open only to nationals of the 26 listed EU member states; non-EU applicants are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Eligible areas of study: Culture & Heritage; Education, Pedagogy; French Language and Civilization, Foreign Languages and Civilizations and European Studies; Law and Political Sciences; Health; Environmental Sciences; Computer Science and Digital.
official.duration: A maximum of 12 months when enrolling in Master 2 and a maximum of 24 months when enrolling in Master 1; the stay must begin between 1 September and 31 December of the year the scholarship is awarded and no deferral is possible.
official.description: Developed by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and managed by Campus France, the France Excellence Europa scholarship programme allows students from 26 European Union countries to obtain scholarships to study at the Master's level in a French institution of higher education.
official.program_type: Government scholarship of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, managed by Campus France

English requirement (no published score; French or English language certificates are optional attachments only)
verification.notes: Amounts (EUR 6,850 half-yearly allowance and EUR 1,700 installation allowance) confirmed on both the programme page and the rights-and-obligations page updated 12 August 2026 on campusfrance.org; the 30 April 2025 deadline comes from the official 2025 call pages.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a living-cost grant, not a full ride: EUR 6,850 per half-year plus a EUR 1,700 arrival payment covers maintenance, while course fees and all travel stay on you and only registration fees for a national degree at public institutions are waived. Applications go by email to the French embassy in your country of nationality, and admission to a French Master 1 or Master 2 is effectively a precondition, so your French university applications must run in parallel with the scholarship file. The last published round closed on 30 April 2025, so track the Campus France programme page for the next call instead of relying on dates circulating on aggregator sites.
applicant_utility.best_fit: EU nationals outside France with strong academic records who have secured, or are close to securing, a French Master's admission and need help with living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Advance a Master 1 or Master 2 admission in France first; without the letter you must attach one sworn statement per intended programme plus proof your admission application is in progress
Have diplomas and transcripts officially translated into French or English before the call opens
Confirm your country's fee.<country>@campusfrance.org embassy address from the programme page and verify the mailbox is active

Prepare the signed application form plus a French or English CV and cover letter, and attach any DELF, DALF, TCF, TEF, TOEFL, TOEIC or IELTS certificates you hold (optional, but they strengthen the file)
Forward the admission letter separately the moment it arrives, since it is due as soon as received rather than with the initial file
common_rejection_risks: Holding any French higher education degree, or being currently registered in France for one, which is an automatic disqualification
Being a French national or a bi-national, including through one parent
Already holding a master's degree from any country, since the no-age-limit rule only applies to applicants without one
Proposing a field of study outside the seven eligible areas listed on the programme page
Missing the email deadline because the file was held back waiting for an admission letter that did not arrive in time
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Course fees (only administrative registration fees for a national degree at public institutions are exempted), CROUS residence rent, all international and national transportation, and daily living costs beyond the EUR 6,850 half-yearly allowance.
document_audit: Diplomas and transcripts must be translated into French or English; untranslated originals are a common reason files are set aside
Each intended programme without an admission letter needs its own sworn statement and its own correspondence trail
The application form must be signed, and the CV and cover letter may be in French or English
Keep the admission letter out of the deadline package but ready to send immediately afterwards
alerts: The stay must start between 1 September and 31 December of the award year and no deferral is possible, so work your admission calendar backwards from that window
Signing an apprenticeship or professional contract automatically terminates the scholarship and all its benefits
Only one gap year is permitted, must be requested at least two months in advance, and the return must be announced by 31 July of the return year
Results are notified subject to admission and the final list was only completed in July for the 2025 round, so visa and housing planning must tolerate months of uncertainty
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email the complete file to your nationality's French embassy; embassies pre-select, the Ministry's field specialists then evaluate and rank the files, and results are published on a main and a complementary list about four weeks after the deadline.

official.deadline_note: 2026 campaign: online entry of files by pre-selected students on the Cascade application ran from 16 February to 12 March 2026 (Circulaire n°593 of 7 January 2026); 2027 campaign dates are not yet published.
official.status_note: The published 2026 campaign window (16 February - 12 March 2026) has closed; AEFE convenes the selection commission each May and the next campaign's dates were not published at verification time.
official.tuition_coverage_note: For holders selected from 2023, the monthly allowance rates are topped up by defined complementary benefits covering round-trip travel and a CROUS university residence place; AEFE does not list course fees among them (tuition-fee coverage was part of the system for holders selected before 2023).
benefits: Monthly allowance of EUR 860 per month at rate 2, or EUR 280 per month at rate 1, allocated according to family situation (holders selected from 2023)
Automatic affiliation for all holders to the complementary health insurance (mutuelle) offered by Campus France
Defined complementary benefits for rate 1 and rate 2 holders: coverage of round-trip travel and reservation of a CROUS university residence place
Status of French government scholarship holder, which facilitates visa, residence permit and university housing procedures

Administrative and financial management of the scholarship by Campus France, plus AEFE follow-up throughout the studies: a sponsorship system, welcome meetings and a departure ceremony for final-year students
eligibility: Is enrolled in classe de terminale in a homologated French school abroad (etablissement d'enseignement francais a l'etranger)
Presents an orientation project in French higher education in a programme awarding a diploma recognised by the State
Wishes to commit to demanding studies from the baccalaureate
Submits orientation wishes on the Parcoursup portal or via specific institutional procedures, identical to those in the scholarship application
Shows genuine motivation and capacity to adapt to life in France
Is pre-selected by the proviseur or proviseure of the French school abroad
For definitive award: obtains the baccalaureate with a 'tres bien' mention and confirms enrolment in the announced track
requirements: The file, entered online by the pre-selected student on the dedicated Cascade application, is evaluated by the service de cooperation et d'action culturelle of the French embassy in the country concerned

It is then examined by AEFE, which submits it to a selection commission composed of higher-education specialists and representatives of excellence tracks (classes preparatoires aux grandes ecoles, grandes ecoles, universities) together with representatives of AEFE and the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
The selection commission is organised by AEFE each year, around May
Definitive attribution is conditioned on obtaining the baccalaureate with a 'tres bien' mention and on confirmation of enrolment in the track announced in the application
documents: Application file entered online by the pre-selected student on the dedicated Cascade application
Baccalaureate result showing the 'tres bien' mention, required for definitive attribution of the scholarship
Confirmation of enrolment in the higher-education track announced in the application
selection_criteria: Involvement in school life or in extracurricular activities
Motivation for demanding higher education studies in France
Ranking of all candidates by an AEFE selection commission held each May
coverage: Monthly allowance of EUR 280 (rate 1) or EUR 860 (rate 2) per month according to family situation, for holders selected from 2023
Complementary health insurance affiliation through the mutuelle offered by Campus France
For rate 1 and rate 2 holders: coverage of round-trip travel and reservation of a CROUS university residence place
application_method: Candidates must be pre-selected by the head (proviseur or proviseure) of the French school abroad before any file can be entered
The pre-selected student enters the file online on the dedicated Cascade application during the published campaign window (16 February - 12 March 2026 for the 2026 campaign)
The French embassy's cultural cooperation and action service evaluates the file, which AEFE then submits to the selection commission convened in May
official.application_route: Be pre-selected by your school head in terminale, then enter the file online on the Cascade application during the February-March campaign window.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must not hold French nationality.
official.international_eligibility: Non-French nationals enrolled in the final year (terminale) of a homologated French school abroad in the AEFE network; the programme serves students of French schools worldwide rather than residents of France.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No disciplinary restriction: any programme in French higher education awarding a State-recognised diploma is eligible, including classes preparatoires, grandes ecoles and universities, provided the orientation project is coherent.
official.duration: Five years of study in France, referenced by AEFE to the time needed to obtain a Master 2 or equivalent.
official.description: France Excellence-Major is a French government mobility scholarship operated by AEFE for the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs: about 850 foreign holders sit across the five annual cohorts, with around 200 new holders joining each year after their terminale year at a French school abroad, and the scholarship runs for five years of higher education in France, with administrative and financial management delegated to Campus France.
official.region: Europe (catalogue region); the programme serves students of French schools abroad worldwide
official.program_type: Government scholarship of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, operated by AEFE with administrative and financial management by Campus France

applicant_utility.summary: This programme only exists inside the French-schools-abroad network: you must be a non-French terminale student pre-selected by your school head before a Cascade file can even be opened, so the practical first move is talking to your proviseur early in your final year. The money is a monthly allowance set by family situation, EUR 860 at rate 2 or EUR 280 at rate 1, plus health cover and, at either rate, round-trip travel and a shot at a CROUS room, while course fees stay on you. Winning a place at the May commission is not the finish line: the award only becomes definitive when you take the baccalaureate with a 'tres bien' mention and confirm enrolment in the exact track you named, so your Parcoursup wishes must mirror your scholarship file.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-performing non-French students in their final year at an AEFE-homologued French school abroad whose families need support to study in France.
application_readiness_checklist: Raise pre-selection with your proviseur as early as possible in terminale; without it there is no route into the application
Make your Parcoursup or institutional orientation wishes identical to the wishes declared in the scholarship file
Prepare transcripts and supporting material before the short February-March Cascade window opens, since the whole file is entered online in that period
Aim for a 'tres bien' baccalaureate mention, because the definitive award is conditional on it
Confirm enrolment in the exact announced track as soon as admission results allow
common_rejection_risks: No pre-selection by the school head, or missing the two-to-three week Cascade entry window
A mismatch between the wishes on Parcoursup and those declared in the scholarship file
Taking the baccalaureate without the 'tres bien' mention, which voids a commission selection
Enrolling in a different track from the one announced in the application
A thin school-life, extracurricular or orientation record, since these are explicit ranking axes alongside results
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and course fees, which are not among the complementary benefits for holders selected from 2023, plus daily living costs beyond the monthly allowance and anything outside the defined round-trip travel benefit and CROUS housing reservation.
document_audit: The definitive-award evidence is the baccalaureate result showing 'tres bien' plus proof of enrolment in the announced track; have both ready over the summer
The full Cascade document list is set out in the 2026 circular and its annexes on aefe.gouv.fr; download and check it before the window opens rather than improvising
Keep screenshots of both Parcoursup and the scholarship file to catch any divergence between the declared wishes
alerts: The 2026 window ran 16 February - 12 March 2026 with the commission in May; 2027 dates are not yet published, so check the AEFE resources page from January onwards
Selection by the commission does not guarantee funding: the award is conditional on the 'tres bien' mention and enrolment in the announced track
The allowance level depends on family situation, so the published EUR 860 is the top rate rather than a guaranteed amount
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The school head pre-selects, the student enters the file on Cascade during the campaign window, the French embassy's cultural service assesses it, AEFE's commission ranks the files in May, and Campus France then handles payment and administration.
